author.name: Efficiency Emilia
author.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.

challenge.name: The Silent Store Gap
challenge.description: A batch of till scan lines from the northern stores was silently dropped during last night's ingestion, causing the model to forecast zero demand for fresh produce. #reliability_ruth# argues that the ingestion pipeline must be fully automated to guarantee every store's data arrives on time, while #data_dave# is willing to accept a manual verification step to ensure data quality before it reaches the feature store.

output.content: I want to be clear about the direction we need to take with our data validation. I am asking for this process to be fully automated. My goal is to improve overall operational efficiency and reduce the manual effort currently spent on checking incoming store data. The more of this work we can shift to automated checks, the better it is for our team. I see no value in keeping a manual verification step in the loop. I want the system to handle the validation so we can focus on strategy rather than data hygiene. This is a clear priority for me, and I expect us to move toward full automation as quickly as possible.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states a desire for full automation to improve efficiency and reduce manual effort, indicating that increasing the level of automation beyond the minimum would make them happier.
